bib.title: Measuring Coding Challenge Competence With APPS
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks

question: How well can language models write Python code from arbitrary natural-language problem specifications, measured by test cases?
contributions: APPS: 10,000 Python problems from introductory to competition level with 131,777 test cases and 232,421 human solutions
Test-case-based metrics (test case average, strict accuracy) and evidence that BLEU is a poor proxy
Evaluation of GPT-2, GPT-Neo and few-shot GPT-3 showing syntax errors fall exponentially with scale/fine-tuning

method.summary: Problems scraped from coding sites (Codewars, AtCoder, Kattis, Codeforces, plus CodeChef, HackerRank, LeetCode) with custom parsers, dedup, and a unified judge. GPT-2 (pretrained on 30 GB decontaminated GitHub Python) and GPT-Neo are fine-tuned on the APPS train set and evaluated by running generated code on test cases; GPT-3 davinci instruct is evaluated few-shot.

datasets.name: APPS
datasets.size: 10,000 problems; 131,777 test cases; 232,421 ground-truth solutions; avg 293.2 words per problem
datasets.split: 5,000 train / 5,000 test; test: 1,000 introductory, 3,000 interview, 1,000 competition; avg 21.2 test cases per test problem
datasets.source: Open-access coding sites; CC BY-SA 3.0 data, MIT code; Fair Use for non-Kattis content
datasets.preprocessing: custom HTML parsers per source, MathPix for equation images to LaTeX, problems needing images removed, tf-idf + SVD cosine dedup, identifying info in solution comments removed; six months of student curation

datasets.name: GitHub Python (GPT-2 pretraining)
datasets.source: GitHub repos with at least one star
datasets.preprocessing: removed repos matching a keyword list (e.g. leetcode, codeforces, solution, code, problem), dropped code with functions sharing APPS starter-code signatures; spaces converted to tabs

models.name: GPT-2 0.1B
models.init_from: GPT-2 then pretrained on GitHub, fine-tuned on APPS

models.name: GPT-2 1.5B
models.init_from: GPT-2 then pretrained on GitHub, fine-tuned on APPS

models.name: GPT-Neo 2.7B
models.init_from: Pile-pretrained (includes GitHub, not decontaminated for APPS), fine-tuned on APPS

training.objective: predict the entire code solution given problem text and format; starter code excluded from loss

other.scope: same optimizer, batch size, weight decay across pretraining and fine-tuning

inference.decoding: HuggingFace default generation parameters except beam search, beam size 5
inference.samples: Top-1: one program; Top-5: best of the 5 beams; one run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Call-based and standard-input prompt templates; GPT-3 few-shot with two example question/solution pairs per format, using shortest passing solutions

metrics.name: Test case average
metrics.definition: mean over problems of fraction of test cases where generated code output equals expected

metrics.name: Strict accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of problems whose generated code passes every test case

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: max BLEU against any human-written solution for the problem

eval.protocol: Run generated code via merged judge; syntax errors identified by whether pyext can load the code as a module; false-positive check on 2- and 3-test-case problems solved by GPT-Neo.

prompts.text:
"
QUESTION:
" + q_str + "
" + starter_code_str + "
" + "
Use Call-Based Format

ANSWER:
" (standard input problems replace Call-Based Format with Standard Input Format)

results.claim: GPT-Neo 2.7B gets about 15% test case average and about 4% strict accuracy on introductory problems (top-1).
results.setup: APPS test split (5,000 problems), fine-tuned on APPS train, beam search size 5, top-1, introductory, test case average
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-Neo 2.7B, column Introductory (Test Case Average)

results.claim: GPT-Neo 2.7B overall strict accuracy is about 1.12% top-1.
results.setup: APPS test split (5,000 problems), fine-tuned on APPS train, beam search size 5, top-1, all difficulty levels
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-Neo 2.7B, column Average (Strict Accuracy)

results.claim: Best of five beams lifts GPT-Neo introductory strict accuracy from 3.9% to 5.5% and test case average from 14.7% to 19.9%.
results.table: Table 3, row Strict Accuracy, column Top-5

results.claim: Top-5 test case average of GPT-2 0.1B (10.75) exceeds top-1 of GPT-2 1.5B (7.96): sampling several candidates is a strong improvement.
results.setup: APPS test, overall average test case average
results.quote: top-5 test case average GPT-2 0.1B is 10.75 while the top-1 test case average of GPT-2 1.5B is 7.96

results.claim: Few-shot GPT-3 175B solves only 3 of 5,000 test problems (two introductory, one interview); strict accuracy 0.06%.
results.setup: GPT-3 davinci instruct, few-shot with two examples per format, APPS test 5,000 problems
results.quote: GPT-3 only solves 3 problems out of 5,000

results.claim: About 59% of GPT-3's introductory solutions have syntax errors vs about 3% for GPT-Neo.
results.setup: introductory problems; syntax error = pyext cannot load the code as a module
results.quote: approximately 59% of GPT-3's generated solutions for introductory problems have syntax errors

results.claim: BLEU is anticorrelated with accuracy: GPT-2 0.1B scores 26.8 introductory BLEU vs GPT-Neo 2.7B 27.1, and BLEU rises with difficulty while accuracy falls.
results.setup: introductory problems, max BLEU against human solutions
results.quote: GPT-2 0.1B has 26.8, 29.7, and 30.2 as BLEU scores for introductory, interview, and competition problems

results.claim: False positives from 2-test-case problems are under 1% of problems (8 of 12 solved ones were false positives).
results.setup: GPT-Neo 2.7B, manual check of problems with 2 test cases
results.quote: the false positive rate with 2 test cases is 8/(890 −4) = 0.009 < 1%

results.claim: Codex 12B (Chen et al. 2021) reaches 4.14% top-1 and 9.65% top-5 introductory accuracy and 25% at top-1000.
results.setup: introductory, Codex 12B, as evaluated by Chen et al. (2021)
results.quote: achieve top-1 and top-5 accuracy on introductory problems of 4.14% and 9.65% respectively

results.claim: GPT-2 1.5B strict accuracy overall is 0.68% top-1; competition-level strict accuracy is 0.00 for all fine-tuned models.
results.setup: APPS test split (5,000 problems), fine-tuned on APPS train, beam search size 5, top-1
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-2 1.5B, column Average (Strict Accuracy)

limits: Few test cases for some Kattis problems (as few as 2) can yield false positives; authors measured under 1% rate.
GPT-Neo pretraining data not decontaminated against APPS; authors argue memorisation is implausible because performance tracks difficulty, but offer no direct test.
GPT-3 evaluated only few-shot with two examples; the 3 solved problems may be memorised or lucky.
Unclear whether GPT-Neo's edge over GPT-2 comes from more code, size or architecture (not disentangled).
Python only; fine-tuning hyperparameters (lr, schedule, seq len) not given; single run, no seeds or intervals.
Dated: 2021 models; Codex and later models far exceed these numbers. Test case coverage is a subset of possible cases.
